top_choice_rationale: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis is chemical at its core (reversible 3'-blocked fluorescent terminators, surface attachment and clonal cluster amplification, single-molecule-level optical readout), has been reproduced on every major platform for about twenty years, and the Balasubramanian-Klenerman pair is the cleanest allocation I can defend, though Rothberg, Ju and Mayer claims and the chemistry-versus-genomics objection are real. I rank Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling second as the better-attributed and better-supported alternative, then the two degrader trios, then the Vancouver lipid trio, and no award last.
